summary: This article explains how the six simple machines, such as the lever, pulley, and ramp, make work easier by trading less force for a longer distance.
introduce: Write the key term “fulcrum” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to guess what it means. Share a few guesses, then tell students to find the word in “Simple Machines Make Work Easier” and check whether they were right.

keyTerms.def: the point that a lever turns on
the force or hard work you put into doing something
sloping up or down, not flat

challengeTerms.def: to use force or strength to do something
something that helps you or puts you in a better position
the spiral ridge that winds around a screw or a lid

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that machines make work easier without any cost at all? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a lever or an inclined plane makes work easier.
struggling: Pre-teach fulcrum, effort, and inclined with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers draw a quick picture for each term and use it in a short spoken sentence.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses exert, advantage, and thread to teach the class one of the terms with their own example.
